arithmetic: 30 * 24 = 720 hours; 0.361 * 0.65 = 0.23465; 0.361 * 720 * 0.65 = 168.94800; rounding the last value to two decimal places (ROUND_HALF_UP) gives 168.95.
formula_scope: An assumed constant hourly price multiplied by assumed rented fraction gives an illustrative amount per calendar GPU-hour. Multiply by GPU count and 720 hours for a 30-day illustration. A population median price times population average utilization is not the observed average of actual host revenue or a forecast for one machine.
comparison: At assumed price $0.50/hour and 20% utilization the amount is $0.10/calendar-hour; at $0.30/hour and 80% utilization it is $0.24/calendar-hour. Thus a higher price can produce a lower illustrative amount.
exclusions: This compute-only illustration models no separate storage/bandwidth/volume revenue, operating cost, tax, fees, payout timing or individual host downtime adjustment. Historical population utilization is an input proxy, not a guarantee of future occupancy.
